title: Good Indices in a Digit String
summary: Given a string s made of digits, identify indices i where a substring ending at i matches the decimal representation of i.
statement: Given a string s made of digits, identify indices i where a substring ending at i matches the decimal representation of i. Return these indices in ascending order as an integer array.
constraints: s contains up to 100,000 decimal digits.
Index i is good when the decimal text of i appears as the suffix ending exactly at s[i].
Return good indices in increasing order.
hints: The candidate text at index i is fixed: str(i).
Its only possible matching substring ending at i begins at i-len(str(i))+1.
Check that this start is nonnegative and compare exactly that slice.
Every good index must use this unique suffix, so the direct scan is exhaustive and ordered.
editorial: Every good index must use this unique suffix, so the direct scan is exhaustive and ordered.

tests.explanation: The suffixes ending at indices zero, eleven, and twelve equal 0, 11, and 12.
Each one-digit index matches the digit at its own position.
